Thank you Pocketpair, for making this game.

I've loved Pokemon my entire life, and I've been a fan of survival sandbox games since the initial, free version of Minecraft's alpha version. What you've done here is create an beautiful quilt of genre blending, with an obvious love for each of them. The irreverent and adult humor is refreshing, and something that as a Pokemon enthusiast, I've desperately needed. For an early access game, it's gorgeous, polished, and something I hope will be relevant for years.

The extremely rare (just look at the positive review percentage) accusations of "AI generation," "3d model theft," or "inappropriate content," are just the petty, jealous, and hateful masses who typically have nothing positive to add to a conversation, and should be left to shout alone into the void.

This game is beautiful, and we needed it. Pocketpair, please don't lose the vision you had for this game. It's flawless the way it is.

It's not "pokemon but edgy", that's the whole wrong genre. it's a survival adventure game where pals are a particularly colorful and fun resource to collect when you go on little adventures away from your base. Then you return to your base, build some more new stuff, and repeat. It's much more like a minecraft or a valheim than any pokemon game imo. (Which means it's as addictive as both put together lol. I played like 36 hours in the first weekend I had it.)

I got it when it first came out so it was hella laggy, but the gameplay and exploration was super fun. If the game feels too slow for you, then you can go into settings and change some stats so that pals are easier to catch, or grinding doesn't take as long. Playing with friends has also gotten so much better as bugs were fixed and all that.

Everyday this game makes me glad they won the lawsuit against Game Freak. Their game is one of the most enjoyable open world, base builders with Pals. I genuinely enjoy all the designs and the Palpedia entries as they are very detailed and entertaining. Some are more dark but it fits the universe! I cannot wait for this game to get out of Alpha and be released in full! I would always recommend it and it's been a blast to play with friends!

It's just a really fun game with a lot to explore and grind for, especially when you hit the higher levels. It brings a massive sense of accomplishment whenever a huge milestone is hit, whether if it's something put in place by the game or a goal you set for yourself

First time I played this game it was in Alpha. It had potential but playing it with friends was so much more trouble than it was worth. Now, they have many so many quality of life improvements and made a game I enjoy and look forward to playing with others. If you are looking for your next survival/collection open world game, give this a try! There are so many corners of the map I love to explore, and there's new stuff I learn with every save and every batch of friends I've played with.

This is everything I wish another popular Japanese game series would've been. A little glitchy on occasion but overall some of the most fun I've had, each aspect of advancing in this is so fun and satisfying. The in-game mechanics are hilarious and thoughtful, the unlocking system is logical and satisfying, the Pals are iconic and the reward system is, well, rewarding. I can see room for some minor improvements while this is in early access - especially building and operating the base but they might be fixable with mods I haven't tried yet so overall 9.5/10 I've been sucked in for daaaaaaaaaaaaays.

I really enjoy playing this game, obviously its still in it's "early stage" and still being developed, but it's definitely a game that I feel like once you get past all the early "in-game" help and stuff, that you might just get as hooked to it as I am. Like, yea, I love Pokemon, and its pretty similar but its more challenging and you have the option to change the game settings whenever you please! The only thing that i would PERSONALLY like to be put in the game, is that instead of having to destroy objects to move them into a different spot is to have to option to "MOVE" or "DISMANTLE" said object. Other than that, great game and I cant wait to see what more comes for this game!

I've dreamt of enslaving the masses since my childhood, back when I was invested in 2b2t. What better way to fulfil that dream than to use the ever-so-familiar format of Pokemon? battle bosses, thugs and wildlife; victory comes with the reward of enslaving the loser (if you choose so) and you also have the option to slave Humans. What's the best part of it all? you can make them breed by force-feeding them cake.
Palworld is the kind of game adults who grew up playing RPGS will enjoy. Nintendo can cry all they want but this game is not Pokemon, Nintendo could never make a game that's this good.

I'd been ignoring this as a clone of that famous Japanese IP, but a friend set me straight; this is a grown-up survival-crafting game using the gimmick of capturing and summoning creatures to *help* in combat and around base. The Pals add some extra layers of strategy and planning.

I think it's the most fun with an open-world survival-crafting game I've had since I first started playing Minecraft with my then-9yp boy. (Although I also loved Abiotic Factor just as much, but it's very much not in the normal vein for survival-crafting games.)

One thing I'm still a little unclear on is how it would work multiplayer; MP is apparently very popular and I started playing this to see if it would be the next game for our weekly group, but for example it seems like the "story" told in the quests is not very deep to engage a group, you'd mostly just be progressing together and choosing your own objectives. I'm breaking my usual policy of disabling comments on this review to see if folks can give an explanation of why it's fun MP.

I've wanted to play this game for a long time, when 1.0 came out it was also on sale, so I knew I had to grab it finally!
I don't have much to say about this game yet besides the fact that its incredibly fun so far.
I find myself saying "It's so cute!" to every single Pal, especially the Kelpsea which is a close sibling to one of my all time favourite creatures from another very popular monster-taming game. (Lapras).
I immediately decided I wanted to rush to level 15 to get the fishing rod - which I've since unlocked.
So now I'll probably spend my time fishing for now ahaha.
There's tons of NPCs that give you quests, bounties, a tech tree - which allow you to unlock things like a 'grapling gun' (which is super fun to use btw), bosses, and many other things to do.
I have been playing with my boyfriend and his little brother and its been super fun!
Though I imagine if you played solo it would be a equally fun experience.
I have experienced some stutters but its probably because of my nearly 10 year old computer. It's crazy to me that I haven't experienced any issues with any of the hardware to this day.
Anyway, as of the timing of this review, it is on sale for another 17 hours so I definitely recommend buying it now.

Unironically great game. Significant bug fixing throughout development have made the gameplay far more stable, resolving most complaints I would have had with the game upon release.

Although the game is often compared to Pokémon for the monster collection component and for its design elements, the gameplay is much closer to ARK: Survival Evolved with some more forgiving features (captured Pals do not die in combat).

Overall, I would recommend giving the game a shot.

After uhming and ahhing about the game for a few months i finally caved and thought id give it a shot. best decision i ever made.

there is so much content early on that keeps you engaged for long periods. the thrill from catching your first little guy is something i cant explain. the visuals are stunning and most importantly there are elements to the game that everyone will enjoy. (i'll get into that a bit more)

Either it be your into combat or farming the game has both those elements. they have made it so if you are someone who doesn't enjoy combat and preffers farming, base building ect, you can still get enough xp to level up and continue to progress through the game.

The combat is thrilling and doesnt feel like your fighting a brick wall, each boss having its own unique mechanics and each fight feels different.

one small thing ive noticed which isn't a huge issue but ive noticed a little bit of rubber banding. which again isn't a huge issue and hasn't caused me to lose any progress, it's more just annoying when i get taken back to a spot i just run from.

but overall i really recommend this game :)

Palworld is one of those rare games that feels both wildly creative and endlessly replayable. It blends the charm of creature collecting with survival, crafting, and base-building mechanics in a way that’s refreshingly unique. Also, this game manages to be relaxing and intense at the same time, and every session leaves you with stories to tell. It’s quirky, fun, and a must-play for fans of open-world adventures who aren’t afraid to embrace a little chaos along the way.

A rare early access gem

Palworld, while still in its development stages, presents players with a vast array of content while also giving you an enjoyable experience overall, which is not something usually found in most early-access games

An area where Palworld could use improvement drastically in is the AI of pals and their pathing. They will sometimes get stuck in trees, random furniture, find themselves somewhere high and drop to their death or just completely stop working. Even while attacking, Pals will just walk off or forget to attack.
It's also worth noting that Palworld seems primarily geared towards a multiplayer experience. Not really a big deal, but I would recommend adjusting your world settings if you find the grind to be too overwhelming.

In conclusion, Palworld shows great promise. While solo play is not as robust or adequately planned for, it still delivers a satisfying experience . With further development and refinement, Palworld has the potential to become a great game for both multiplayer and single-player.

Palworld has mad some serious progress since its first release and if you are looking for a reason to get back into it, the free DLC islands and major additions to the research, and new base additions make it well worth the time. I personally enjoy the deep dive that is pal breeding but to each their own. The second DLC island is such a blast and a welcomed increase in difficulty with more creative pals, boss fights. and challenging terrain to navigate. The game does still need some work with some areas of the map feeling a little baron or empty such as the desert area and some of the ice area but hopefully more work will be done their in the future. I look forward to the endgame world tree and whatever that might entail. I would really like to see the ability to throw out your pals to come back but not much we can do about that one.
It's a much more complicated game that just Pokemon with guns. It is a very engaging progression game.
